prompt:
High-fidelity mobile UI design comp: one portrait phone screen filling the frame.

The app is Squirrel, a personal memory aid. This screen is its "chores" room, designed as a 1960s French yé-yé pop record sleeve.

STRUCTURE, top to bottom:
1. The entire screen is one flat saturated tangerine-orange ground (#e66d0d), edge to edge, no panels and no cards.
2. At the head, a rounded heavy lowercase logotype in near-black (#1c110b) reading "the chores", set large and tight. Beneath it, tiny wide-tracked uppercase monospace: "SQUIRREL · SIDE ONE · ONE WAITING".
3. In the middle, a perfect square crop occupying most of the width, filled flat deep purple (#3b2560), with the chore name set inside it in enormous condensed heavy uppercase cream (#fed6a7) lettering across three lines: "WATER THE PLANTS". The square has a hairline near-black edge.
4. At the foot, four track lines ranked in a tidy block, each a thin near-black rule above it, each line a tiny monospace catalogue number at left and a title at right in medium-weight condensed type:
   A1 "DID IT" — set in white (#fffbf3), the active one
   A2 "HOW OFTEN IT COMES BACK" — near-black
   A3 "STOP ASKING" — near-black
   A4 "BINS OUT — DONE" — near-black at 45 percent opacity, a played track

MATERIALS: flat offset-printed ink, no gradients, no shadows, no texture. Absolutely flat colour fields.
STRICT PALETTE: #e66d0d #3b2560 #fed6a7 #1c110b #fffbf3.
TYPE: a rounded geometric pop logotype at the head; condensed grotesque for the track titles; tiny monospace for catalogue numbers.
MOOD: a record sleeve on a rack — confident, graphic, one saturated colour owning the whole surface. Not an app, not a card layout, no rounded rectangles floating on a background.
